text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm seeing steady memory growth in the KV cache on longctx repros (16k+ tokens). Runs that used to plateau now keep climbing over ~30m. attaching quick trace + heap diff.
kevin: repro? single-request longctx or many short requests stitched?
maria: single request (chat history expansion) + repeating prefixes across segments. repro script: `tests/longctx/regen_kv_growth.py` — I pushed logs to the thread.
perf-bot: New profile uploaded: https://perf.internal/reports/1768456789 (flamegraph + heap diff)
jess: quick glance: flamegraph shows a lot of small allocations in the KV slab allocator, and >50% of entries are <1KB. sounds like fragmentation to me.
kevin: what's the cache key format we're using for those runs? could be over-specified per-session and preventing reuse.
maria: current key format (simplified):
```
<model>:<ver>|sess:<session_id>|prefix_hash:<sha1_prefix>|pos:<start_pos>
```
that's what I used in the repro.
sam: that includes pos — that will poison reuse. if prefix_hash is identical across requests but pos differs, we treat them as separate entries. we probably intended pos for partial re-use but longctx creates many unique pos values.
jess: agreed. we originally added pos to avoid serving stale KV slices for overlapping windows, but for repeated prefixes we should canonicalize to prefix-only keys and store offsets within the value.
kevin: also noticed kernel selection change from the 1767xx rollout altered attention chunking (different kernel emits different per-token KV chunk sizes). that interacts with allocator alignment and causes more small allocations -> fragmentation.
maria: profiler shows allocator churn spikes right after kernel switch + higher eviction churn. Eviction policy is LRU with soft-TTL of 10m; but because of key explosion, we never hit good locality and evict warm prefixes.
perf-bot: Heap diff: +220MB over 30m, 62% attributable to KV slab fragmentation, 28% to live KV entries.
sam: short-term mitigation options:
- normalize keys: drop `pos` for prefix cache keys, keep session-scoped keys only for session-level sticky features
- coalesce small KV chunks into a packed slab object
- bump eviction aggressiveness for small entries (treat small entries as lower priority)
- revert kernel change that affects chunk size until allocator tuning done
kevin: preference: 1) normalize keys (low risk) 2) pack small chunks (medium) 3) revert kernel (high impact) — we can A/B the kernel revert on canary
maria: I ran a quick patch that normalizes prefix keys to `model:ver|prefix_hash:<sha1>` and maps `pos` into an index in the value. in local sim the growth stops and reuse ratio jumps from 22% -> 78% for repeated prompts.
jess: nice. please open a PR and include the simple serialization change + migration path. add a feature flag so Dedicated customers can opt in/out for safety.
maria: will do. PR draft: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/12345 (wip)
kevin: follow-ups: can we add a daily job to scan for high-unique-key patterns and alert? this could catch regressions earlier.
sam: +1. also add metric: `kv_prefix_reuse_rate` and `kv_fragmentation_ratio` (heap-allocated / live-value-size).
maria: added TODOs to the PR. I'll also run a canary with kernel revert vs key-normalize to measure latency/throughput impact.
jess: sounds good. quick note — if we pack small chunks, watch CPU decode cost when reading packed entries (more memcpy). weigh tradeoffs.
maria: noted. I'll capture end-to-end perf (p99 latency + cost/token) in the experiment.
kevin: thanks. resolving for now, keep thread updated with PR / canary numbers. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: Incident detection: kv-fragmentation alert cleared after key-normalize patch in local sim (not production).
